articles.title: Govt Advances Geothermal Energy Plans In The Andamans | Nation - Ommcom News
articles.content: Kolkata: The government is seriously considering tapping into the geothermal reserves around the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to meet the archipelago’s power requirements. The Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) Ltd has invited Expressions of Interest (EoIs) from agencies to undertake geothermal resource assessment, exploration and potential power plant development in the island chain. Geothermal energy is generated from sub surface steam or hot water. This is non polluting, renewable energy that can be generated round the clock in all weather conditions. The Andamans are presently heavily dependent on diesel imports from the mainland to run generators that produce electricity. The Government is keen to reduce this dependence by generating green energy as conventional power plants are not a possibility in the eco sensitive zone. Geothermal energy is a distinct possibility as the island chain sits directly on a very active tectonic boundary where the major Indian Plate continues to slide beneath the smaller Burma Plate, resulting in seismic activity. South Asia’s only active volcano is also located on Barren Island in the Andaman Islands. The Geological Survey of India has also identified the islands as one of the country’s major geothermal provinces. Given this setting, SECI wants to assess the commercial viability of geothermal energy in the island territory. This forms part of the implementation of the National Policy on Geothermal Energy, notified by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) in September 2025. It now seeks participation from developers, drilling agencies, technology providers, research institutions and integrated energy companies with expertise in geothermal exploration and development. The exercise is intended to identify technically capable agencies for what could become one of India’s first geothermal power projects in an island region. Geothermal energy has the potential to provide indigenous, weather independent baseload renewable power, improving long term energy security for the islands, SECI says. At the moment, India’s theoretical geothermal resource potential is estimated at around 10,600 MW. The country has 381 documented hot springs, with 42 geothermal manifestations identified as promising sites for future exploration. The proposed programme will begin with geological, geophysical and geochemical investigations, followed by exploratory drilling, resource validation and, subject to successful resource confirmation, development of a geothermal power plant. The indicative project capacity is expected to be between 5 MW and 20 MW. The resource assessment and feasibility stage may take around 18 months, while power plant development is expected to require a further 24 months following successful resource validation, SECI has indicated. It has proposed a tariff ceiling of Rs 15 per kWh and a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) tenure of 20–25 years for future competitive bidding. The Electricity Department of the Andaman and Nicobar Administration will procure electricity generated under the project. Both Indian and international entities can participate, either individually or through consortiums. SECI is seeking organisations with experience in geothermal exploration, deep drilling, preferably to depths of 1,000 metres or more, renewable energy project development or integrated infrastructure development. articles.title: AI -Generated Content And Copyright Protection In India: Navigating Authorship, Ownership ...
articles.content: ARTICLE 14 August 2026 AI-Generated Content And Copyright Protection In India: Navigating Authorship, Ownership And Emerging Legal Challenges KS King, Stubb & Kasiva More Contributor King Stubb & Kasiva (KSK) is a full-service law firm with 10 offices nationwide, including New Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune, Kochi, and Mangalore, and a team of 150+ professionals. Explore Firm Details Generative Artificial Intelligence (“AI”) has transformed the way content is created across industries, enabling users to generate text, images, music, software code and audiovisual content within seconds. While these technological advancements have unlocked new opportunities for businesses and creators, they have also raised fundamental questions concerning copyright ownership, authorship and the use of copyrighted works for training AI models. India Intellectual Property Himanshu Deora Your Author LinkedIn Connections To print this article, all you need is to be registered or login on Mondaq.com. Article Insights Himanshu Deora’s articles from King, Stubb & Kasiva are most popular: in India King, Stubb & Kasiva are most popular: within Government, Public Sector, Employment and HR and Criminal Law topic(s) with readers working within the Law Firm industries Introduction Generative Artificial Intelligence (“AI”) has transformed the way content is created across industries, enabling users to generate text, images, music, software code and audiovisual content within seconds. While these technological advancements have unlocked new opportunities for businesses and creators, they have also raised fundamental questions concerning copyright ownership, authorship and the use of copyrighted works for training AI models. India’s copyright framework, primarily governed by the Copyright Act, 1957 (“Act”), was enacted at a time when creative works were inherently associated with human authors. The emergence of autonomous AI systems has exposed gaps in the existing legal framework, particularly regarding whether AI-generated outputs qualify for copyright protection, who owns such works, and whether the use of copyrighted material for AI training amounts to infringement. This article examines the current legal position in India, recent judicial developments, and emerging policy proposals shaping the future of AI and copyright law. The Existing Legal Framework Copyright protection under the Act extends to original literary, dramatic, musical and artistic works, cinematograph films and sound recordings. The concept of authorship remains central to copyright protection, with Section 2(d) identifying the “author” for different categories of protected works. Indian copyright jurisprudence has consistently linked originality to human intellectual effort. In Eastern Book Company v. D.B. Modak 1 , the Supreme Court held that a work must demonstrate a “modicum of creativity” arising from the author’s skill, judgment and intellectual labour to qualify for copyright protection. Although the Act does not expressly address artificial intelligence, Section 2(d)(vi) provides that, in the case of a computer-generated work , the author is “the person who causes the work to be created.” Introduced in 1994, this provision contemplated computer-assisted creation rather than autonomous generative AI. Consequently, its applicability to AI-generated content remains uncertain and has not yet been interpreted by Indian courts in the context of modern generative AI systems. articles.title: Island Computing to launch India's first fully managed sovereign cloud on 15 August
articles.content: Corporate 2 min read Island Computing to launch India’s first fully managed sovereign cloud on 15 August Island Computing will launch its sovereign cloud platform in India on August 15, 2026. This platform ensures data centers and operations remain within India under local laws. It offers rapid environment provisioning and application deployment capabilities. Benchmarks indicate significantly lower costs compared to foreign cloud providers. The service aims to support India's growing tech economy and regulatory needs. ETCIO Desk Agencies Published On Aug 14, 2026 at 08:02 AM IST Select ETCIO as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Island Computing announced that its fully managed sovereign cloud platform will become generally available from August 15, 2026, in India. The platform is designed to keep data centres, hardware, operating entities, cloud operations, control and data planes, identity systems and audit logs within India and under Indian law. It is intended for enterprises, government bodies and developers running workloads that require data localisation and jurisdictional control. Island Computing said its platform can provision an environment in 90 seconds and deploy a production-grade application in three minutes. The company also said a published benchmark workload costs 30% less than equivalent configurations in the AWS Mumbai region, before committed-use or enterprise discounts. Advt According to Island Computing, around 80% of India’s projected $26.4 billion cloud spending in 2026 will flow to AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud and other foreign providers. “India is the fastest-growing tech economy in the world, and that growth deserves infrastructure it fully owns. Sovereignty isn’t a constraint, it’s a competitive advantage, it means our banks, our government, and our builders can move fast without ever giving up control of the stack their future runs on,” said Vishal Sirohi, Founder and CEO, Island Computing. The platform uses a distributed control and data plane designed to provide fault tolerance across data centres. It supports multi-tenant SaaS, long-running agentic workloads and regulated AI applications using Indian data. The infrastructure uses a microVM-based hypervisor for tenant isolation. The company said isolation is enforced during workload admission. The platform also configures network topology, tenant isolation, autoscaling, observability and identity when environments are provisioned. Island Computing said the platform is designed to support India’s regulatory requirements, including provisions related to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, RBI data-localisation requirements, SEBI cloud advisories and CERT-In’s six-hour incident-reporting directive. The company also said the platform complies with the MeitY mandate. Advt The platform will be available from August 15 to enterprises, government bodies and developers across India. Partner onboarding will also begin on the same date for organisations working on BFSI, healthcare, telecommunications, public-sector, IoT, SaaS, video, gaming and agentic AI workloads. articles.title: Kerala Police opens its doors wider with launch of 'My Police Station' - tennews.in
articles.content: National Kerala Police opens its doors wider with launch of ‘My Police Station’ On Aug 14, 2026 Share Thiruvananthapuram, Aug 14 (IANS) Kerala’s 484 police stations will undergo a transformation where people can walk in without hesitation, Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan said on Friday while launching the ‘My Police Station’ initiative at the Peroorkada police station. The initiative seeks to change not merely the appearance of police stations but, more importantly, the way they function and interact with the public. Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala, local MLA and Health Minister K. Muraleedharan, and senior police officials attended the inauguration. “The colour of police stations may become uniform across Kerala, but the real change should be in the way they function,” said Chennithala and stressed that police stations should be places where people feel comfortable seeking help and where their grievances receive due attention. Under the initiative, police stations will have dedicated complaint, women’s, children’s, senior citizens’, transgender, persons with disabilities, cybercrime and legal-aid help desks. Assistance for applications, online services, RTI-related information and obtaining FIR copies will also be made available. Over the years, Kerala Police had consistently adapted itself to technological and social changes and recalled that India’s first women’s police station was established in Kozhikode. “Every citizen should feel free to visit a police station and extend support and cooperation to the police,” he said, pointing to the success of ‘Operation Toofan’, one of the State’s major anti-narcotics drives, as evidence of what could be achieved through public participation. The CM Satheesan government’s objective is to build a people-friendly, technology-driven, accountable and professionally equipped police force that meets international standards. Chennithala also stressed the need for strict adherence to Supreme Court directives on arrests and other police procedures. Referring to custodial deaths that had brought disrepute to the force, he said the government was determined to ensure that such incidents did not occur in future. CCTV cameras have been installed in all police stations to strengthen transparency and accountability. A major change taking effect from Friday is the appointment of young Sub-Inspectors as Station House Officers, with 63 women Sub-Inspectors taking charge as SHOs. Chennithala said the government would give greater attention to the mental well-being of police personnel, including training programmes aimed at preventing suicidal tendencies among officers. “The transformation has already begun,” Chennithala said underlining that Kerala Police must evolve continuously to meet the changing expectations of society. –IANS sg/rad Share Facebook Twitter Google+ ReddIt WhatsApp Pinterest Email

articles.title: Uttar Pradesh: Parichha Weir Gets ICID Heritage Recognition - GKToday
articles.content: Home Uttar Pradesh: Parichha Weir Gets ICID Heritage Recognition Uttar Pradesh: Parichha Weir Gets ICID Heritage Recognition August 13, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 The International Commission on Irrigation and Drainage (ICID) designated the 140-year-old Parichha Weir in Jhansi as a World Heritage Irrigation Structure (WHIS) on 13 August 2026. The structure is linked to the Betwa Canal system, which irrigates land in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. World Heritage Irrigation Structure WHIS is a recognition given by ICID to historic irrigation structures with engineering, cultural, and operational value. ICID is an international body concerned with irrigation, drainage, and flood management, and it maintains a list of heritage irrigation structures from different countries. Parichha Weir: Engineering Features The Parichha Weir is a rubble-stone masonry structure that stretches 1,174 metres and stands 16.8 metres above the riverbed. It uses 318 steel falling shutters and has a reservoir capacity of 2,400 million cubic feet. The Betwa Canal system associated with the weir extends about 2,654 km and irrigates 4,28,360 hectares across five districts in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. The weir is located on the Betwa River in the Jhansi region. Historical Background The canal system was first proposed by Captain Strachey in 1855. Construction began in 1881 at a cost of ₹40 lakh, and the system was commissioned in 1886. The Parichha Weir became the second major structure in the Jhansi region to receive ICID heritage status after the Sukwa-Dukwan Weir was recognised in 2022. Important Facts for Exams ICID stands for the International Commission on Irrigation and Drainage. WHIS refers to World Heritage Irrigation Structure. The Parichha Weir is associated with the Betwa River and the Betwa Canal system. The structure was commissioned in 1886 after construction began in 1881. Related Institutional Context The formal award presentation is scheduled in France during the 26th ICID International Congress and the 77th International Executive Council meeting in October 2026. The Parichha Thermal Power Project is located near the weir, and published capacity figures for the project have varied across records. articles.title: Chandigarh University joins ISRO to host National Space Technology Conclave on 17th-18th August
articles.content: Home ANI Press Releases Chandigarh University joins ISRO to host National Space Technology Conclave on 17th-18th... ANI Press Releases Chandigarh University joins ISRO to host National Space Technology Conclave on 17th-18th August; Group Capt Shubhanshu Shukla among 30 Space Scientists to attend ANI PR 14 August, 2026 10:31 am IST Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Group Capt Shubhanshu Shukla & some of the eminent ISRO Scientists who are going to attend the National Space Technology Conclave 2026 at Chandigarh University Follow Us : Text Size: A- A+ PRNewswire Chandigarh [India], August 14: Giving fresh impetus to India’s growing space ambitions and advancing the Viksit Bharat vision through innovation, indigenous space capabilities and a future-ready scientific workforce, Chandigarh University’s Kalpana Chawla Centre for Research in Space Science and Technology (KCC) is all set to organise India’s first university-led National Space Technology Conclave (NSTC) 2026 on August 17-18 at the University campus. Show Full Article The two-day conclave, being jointly organised in collaboration with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and the Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology (IIST), Department of Space, Government of India will focus on the theme ‘Emerging Space Technologies for India’s Future Space Missions’ and will provide students a direct platform to engage with 30 distinguished scientists, mission leaders and technologists from ISRO, IIST, Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Center (IN-SPACe), NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) and U R Rao Satellite Centre (URSC) with 10 CEOs and senior leaders from leading Indian space industries and start-ups. The conclave will feature five roundtables and space technology demonstrations, facilitating discussions on the technologies shaping India’s next phase of space exploration and human spaceflight while inspiring the next generation of innovators to contribute to the nation’s Viksit Bharat journey. The conclave will feature Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, Ashoka Chakra, Indian astronaut and Indian Air Force officer, as the Special Guest. Group Captain Shukla created history in June 2025 by becoming the first Indian to visit the International Space Station (ISS) and participated in scientific experiments, marking a defining moment in the nation’s space exploration journey. He has also been selected as one of the astronauts for India’s Gaganyaan human spaceflight programme. Among the prominent space scientists and experts expected to participate are Dr Pawan Goenka, Chairman, IN-SPACe, Department of Space; Dr S Somnath, Former Chairman, ISRO; Dr Rajeev Jyothi, Director, Technical Directorate, IN-SPACe, Department of Space; Prof D Banerjee, Vice-Chancellor, IIST, Department of Space; Dr A Bharadwaj, Director, PRL, Department of Space; M Sankaran, Director, URSC, ISRO; Dr RP Singh, Director, IIRS, ISRO; and I S S Sarkar, Director, SAC, ISRO. The wider participation will include senior scientists, directors, project leaders, researchers, technologists, industry leaders and start-up representatives from across India’s space sector. A major outcome of the two-day conclave will be the ‘Chandigarh University Declaration on Space Technology for Viksit Bharat 2047’ which will bring together space scientists, institutional leaders and the Chandigarh University team to define the role and responsibilities of universities in contributing to India’s space technology ambitions....

articles.title: Stuffcool Nido: How good is India's first Qi2.2 wireless power bank? - Digit
articles.content: Home » Feature Story » General » Stuffcool Nido: How good is India’s first Qi2.2 wireless power bank? Stuffcool Nido: How good is India’s first Qi2.2 wireless power bank? By Jayesh Shinde | Updated on 14-Aug-2026 Add DIGIT as a preferred source Follow Us HIGHLIGHTS India's first Qi2.2 power bank promises 25W, delivers considerably less Thermal throttling prevents even Qi2.2 supported phones to charge slowly Well built at Rs 4,999, but the cable outperforms its wireless magnets Jayesh Shinde 14-Aug-2026 Believe me when I say this that magnetic power banks that charge a smartphone wirelessly are one of the best things to have happened. True freedom from charging cables is a joy you can only feel when you experience it. But magnetic power banks don’t equal fast charging, at least wirelessly. And that’s been largely my experience with the Stuffcool Nido. Survey ✅ Thank you for completing the survey! Marketed as India’s first Qi2.2-certified power bank, the 10,000mAh battery packed Stuffcool Nido promises to deliver up to 25W of magnetic wireless charging on compatible smartphones – most iPhones, Pixels, Samsung Galaxy S-series flagships – with the added bonus of 45W of wired PD. It’s a pretty little thing, the Stuffcool Nido. Easy to grip, with a premium look, weighing just 194 gm and barely 1.67-cm thick. It’s small enough to sit comfortably in your jeans pocket or hide neatly inside your backpack – you won’t even notice it. It’s built well, too. It survives shakes, minor drops without any visible damage on the outside. The Stuffcool Nido’s integrated kickstand is a neat addition to the powerbank, allowing it to prop up a phone in portrait mode for video calls easily, among other things. I found it a useful feature on most days for idle browsing on the phone, keeping it propped up on the desk instead of holding it in my palm. Another useful feature of the Stuffcool Nido is its built-in USB-C cable, where a clever design decision allows it to tuck itself and form a loop which can give you extra grip on the powerbank and smartphone combo when they’re magnetically attached. Beyond design and features, when it comes to brass tacks, I tested the Stuffcool Nido extensively for a couple of weeks on an iPhone 15 Pro, Samsung Galaxy S25, and very briefly on an iPhone 17 (barely a day before writing this review). Stuffcool Nido’s performance is a bit of a mixed bag, if you ask me. I started off charging an iPhone 15 Pro at 1%, with the Stuffcool Nido at 100%. Twenty minutes into the charging run, and the iPhone read 21% which was pretty good. I finally thought, yes, this is what the Qi2.2 is supposed to feel like. But that’s where the highs ended, I’m afraid. The next 30% points took as much as 95 mins or 1 hour 35 mins in total. articles.title: Punjab Police's Sadak Surakhya Force to become India's first 3D policing model
articles.content: CHANDIGARH: The Sadak Surakhya Force (SSF), Punjab Police's dedicated highway patrol force for saving the lives of commuters, will integrate drones, satellite imagery and artificial intelligence powered predictive systems in its flagship project, making it India's first 3D policing model. In Phase II of the SSF expansion, the proposed 3D policing model will combine drones, satellite imagery and AI powered predictive systems to create real time situational awareness, anticipate risks and support faster police response, making overall traffic and road safety policing more versatile. It will also extend SSF coverage from the existing 5,500 km to 6,000 km of state roads. The longer term Vision SSF 2047 seeks to build an integrated road safety ecosystem combining satellite data, artificial intelligence, drones and geospatial technologies. Punjab DGP Gaurav Yadav said, "With an aim of digital enforcement integrating Artificial Intelligence and satellite data, the ‘Vision SSF 2047’ includes achieving minimal road accidents, fully green mobility corridors, and establishing regional research hubs under the Punjab Road Safety and Traffic Research Centre (PRSTRC)." "The sole target of this project is making Punjab India's road safety hub using science, systems, and synergy. Punjab Police will use satellite communication and geospatial data for incident mapping, congestion prediction, and disaster management. The SSF is already India's first dedicated force for highway safety." "We are further exploring the possibilities to integrate it with geostationary nano or micro satellite of our own," he added. The SSF project works under various arms, including the Intelligent Transport Management System (ITMS), which serves as the technological backbone by integrating AI, IoT sensors and real time analytics for automated enforcement, smart surveillance and data driven traffic planning. With Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) based enforcement, predictive analytics and mobile interceptors, the police have already achieved an average accident response time of under seven minutes. Under the ‘Road Safety Punjab’ vision, traffic management is being transformed using the 7E Framework: Engineering, Enforcement, Education, Electronics, Emergency Care, Engagement and Evaluation. This strategy marks a shift from intuition based management to an evidence based, technology-driven approach. On the other hand, the PRSTRC leads research, consultancy and training. It is supported by Research Advisory Groups (RAGs) from academia, industry and civil society. Special DGP (Traffic and Road Safety Punjab) Amardeep Singh Rai said, "Regular police are trained for law and order, which is a very different and broad skillset. The SSF, on the other hand, received highly specialised training with a clear, non negotiable priority: saving lives. The SSF personnel were put through specific training modules on emergency response and first aid, including training from the Red Cross, and are trained in ‘crash investigation’." "The entire force is built around one concept: the platinum 10 minutes, which mandates reaching an accident victim within six to eight minutes to provide immediate medical relief before the ambulance or hospital takes over." articles.title: Skyroot deepens aerospace footprint with Tamil Nadu facility - The Hans India
articles.content: Skyroot deepens aerospace footprint with Tamil Nadu facility The Hans India Update: 2026-08-13 22:34 IST Skyroot deepens aerospace footprint with Tamil Nadu facility Hyderabad: Hyderabad-based space-tech unicorn Skyroot Aerospace, maker of India’s first private orbital rocket, will invest Rs 250 crore to set up its first facility in Tamil Nadu at Thoothukudi, creating around 500 jobs. The company will set up the facility for the storage, assembly, integration and testing of its launch vehicles. The MoU with Guidance Tamil Nadu will be signed at the Vetri Conclave here on Thursday in the presence of Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay and exchanged with Deepak Jacob, Managing Director and CEO, Guidance Tamil Nadu. The facility’s location is significant as it is close to the Indian Space Research Organisation’s second spaceport at Kulasekarapattinam, which is targeted to become operational in 2026-27. Skyroot, founded by Pawan Chandana and Naga Bharath Daka, became a unicorn earlier this year and has emerged as one of the most prominent players in India’s private space sector. On July 18, its Vikram-1 completed India’s first private orbital launch, making India only the third country with private orbital launch capability, according to the company. “ Tamil Nadu’s strategic location, the upcoming spaceport at Kulasekarapattinam and its strong industrial ecosystem make it an important part of Skyroot’s next phase of growth. This facility will strengthen our capabilities as we scale the Vikram programme towards a higher launch cadence,” Naga Bharath Daka, Co-founder and CTO, Skyroot Aerospace, said. The investment is part of a broader investment push by Tamil Nadu, with 97 companies signing fresh MoUs at the state government’s first “Vetri Tamil Nadu Investors Conclave 2026”. The pacts involve total investment commitments of more than Rs 67,452 crore and are expected to generate around 1.20 lakh jobs. The MoU is among eight agreements signed at the conclave across aerospace and defence, space and maritime sectors, involving a combined investment of Rs 3,087 crore and creating 6,970 jobs. Other major investments announced at the conclave include Rs 400 crore by Agnikul Cosmos for space technology and launch vehicle assembly in Thoothukudi, Rs 2,500 crore by the Hinduja Group in renewable energy and mobility solutions, and Rs 4,000 crore by Daimler India Commercial Vehicles in Kanchipuram.
